p.title: Together We Can
p.challenge: Put the story in order: how did four children clean the muddy path?

panels.t: The rain washed mud all over the school path in Mysuru.
"It is too much for me," sighed Meera.
Arjun brought a broom, Salma a bucket and Tenzin a spade.
Everyone took one small job.
By lunch, the path was clean. Together we can!

p.title: Dev says No, Go, Tell
p.challenge: Put Dev's story in order. Spot when he says No, goes away and tells

panels.t: After school, Dev waited at the gate for his mother.
A man he did not know said, "Come with me, I have chocolates."
Dev said a loud "No!"
He went back inside the school, a safe place.
He told his teacher, who called his mother.

p.title: One Thing at a Time
p.challenge: Put the lines of the poem in order: first work, then play

panels.t: When I draw, I only draw,
I do not watch TV.
When I read, I only read,
The words come clear to me.
When work is done, I run to play,
And laugh the whole bright day!

p.title: The Old Stag
p.challenge: Put the fable in order, then think: what is the moral?

panels.t: Near the Satpura hills lived Dhruv, an old, slow stag.
The young deer laughed, "You are so slow, grandpa!"
One hot summer, the ponds dried up.
The young deer were thirsty and worried.
Dhruv led them to a hidden spring behind the big rocks.
"We are sorry. You are slow, but you are wise."

p.title: Louis Braille
p.challenge: Put Louis Braille's life in order, oldest first

events.label: Born in France
events.info: Louis Braille was born on 4 January 1809.

events.label: Hurts his eye in an accident
events.info: He was about 3 years old. Soon after, he lost his sight.

events.label: Goes to a school for blind children in Paris
events.info: There were very few books he could read.

events.label: Makes a code of raised dots
events.info: He was only about fifteen. We call it braille.

events.label: Publishes his braille system in a book
events.info: Today people all over the world read braille. World Braille Day is on 4 January, his birthday.

p.title: Anaya's morning yoga
p.challenge: Put Anaya and her grandfather's yoga in order

panels.t: In the morning, Anaya and Grandfather go to the terrace.
They stand tall like a mountain in Tadasana.
They balance on one leg like a tree in Vrikshasana.
They breathe in slowly and breathe out slowly.
"My body feels strong and my mind feels calm!"

p.title: The Lagori Champions
p.challenge: Put the lagori match in order

panels.t: Team Sunflower threw the ball at the pile of seven flat stones.
The pile of stones fell down.
Quickly, they began to stack the stones again.
Team Mango tried to get them out with the ball.
Leela placed the last stone and shouted, "Lagori!"
Team Mango clapped and said, "Well played!"

p.title: Tara's quiet morning
p.challenge: Put Tara's morning in order. Which sense did she use each time?

panels.t: Tara sat quietly under a neem tree in her village in Odisha.
She watched a line of ants carrying tiny crumbs. (seeing)
She heard a bulbul singing on a branch. (hearing)
She smelt the wet earth after the rain. (smelling)
She saw a small snail moving slowly on a leaf. (seeing)

p.title: The Swing
p.challenge: Put the lines of the poem in order. Listen for the rhymes: low–go, sun–fun, sing–swing

panels.t: Under the banyan, my swing hangs low,
Didi gives a push and away I go!
Forward I fly with my toes to the sun,
Back I come laughing, oh, what fun!
The parrots cheer and the breezes sing,
My heart flies high on my happy swing!

p.title: A Journey to the Magical Mountains
p.challenge: Follow Ishaan's journey: put it in order

panels.t: In May, Ishaan's family took the toy train from Kalka to Shimla.
The little train puffed through tunnels and over bridges.
Pine trees stood tall on the slopes.
Far away, Ishaan saw snowy peaks shining in the sun.
That night, it was so cold that he slept under two quilts.
